metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to over-forecast (especially after spikes), so reduce forecast peak values by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply a downward correction of 3–8% to prevent overreaction.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-period, model may lag in adjusting downward; anticipate mean reversion and adjust forecast downward 2–5% in the following 3–5 days.
- Model underestimates true price volatility when sentiment is mixed or neutral; increase forecast range by 1–3% to account for uncertainty.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates mean price; apply a 2–5% downward bias to align with observed mean reversion patterns.
- If sentiment history shows repeated negative sentiment, model tends to overreact to minor price changes; apply smoothing filter to reduce noise in short-term forecasts.
